notes:
CIRCUIT: a four-branch DC ladder. A 10V source (#4) in series with a 10 Ohm resistor (#0) drives a top rail at y~360; hanging off that rail are (a) 5MF capacitor #3 in series with 10k resistor #6 down to the bottom rail, (b) 10k resistor #1 in series with 5H inductor #5 down to the bottom rail, and (c) a 2A current source #2. The bottom rail at y~655 is the ground rail, tied to the GND symbol #7 by the stub that continues below the rail at x~504. 8 components, 5 nets.

NET MAP:
  n1 = between the source and the series resistor: TOP terminal of V-DC #4, LEFT lead of 10 Ohm resistor #0. Physically the x~145 column from y~420 up to the corner at (145,360) and right to x~180.
  n2 = the top rail: RIGHT lead of resistor #0, TOP lead of 10k resistor #1, TOP terminal of I-DC #2, TOP plate of capacitor #3. Runs from x~349 to the corner at (887,360).
  n3 = between 10k #1 and 5H #5: BOTTOM lead of resistor #1 (704,482), TOP lead of inductor #5 (703,501).
  n4 = between 5MF #3 and 10k #6: BOTTOM plate of capacitor #3 (508,481), TOP lead of resistor #6 (505,504).
  0  = the bottom rail plus the GND stub: BOTTOM terminal of V-DC #4, BOTTOM lead of resistor #6, BOTTOM lead of inductor #5, BOTTOM terminal of I-DC #2, GND #7. Runs from the corner at (143,655) to the corner at (881,655), with the stub down from (504,666) to the GND symbol at (505,692).

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all four recorded):
  S4 (702,370) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Plain T: the top rail runs continuously left-right and the resistor #1 branch descends from it. There is no fourth branch, so no crossing reading exists; the branch must join the rail or resistor #1 would float.
  S5 (502,376) deg=3 - JUNCTION. Same geometry for the capacitor branch.
  S7 (709,663) deg=3 - JUNCTION. T with a heavy blob (dot=2.5): the inductor's bottom lead comes down and stops on the bottom rail; nothing continues below. A crossing reading is not available at degree 3, and would leave the R#1/L#5 branch open.
  S8 (504,666) deg=4 - JUNCTION. This is the only genuine four-way on the sheet: the x~504 column passes through the bottom rail and continues down to the GND symbol. inkmap at (504,666) shows a plain X - the column is 4-5px above and 3-4px below, widening only to 7px (about 1.7x) through the crossing, with no hop and no sideways jog, so there is no crossing marker. DECIDED JUNCTION on rule 1 (electrical impossibility of the alternative): if the column merely passed over the rail, net 0 would contain nothing but GND #7 and the bottom lead of resistor #6, so the capacitor/resistor branch would have no return path and could carry no current, and the bottom rail (V-DC, I-DC, inductor) would have no ground reference at all. The ink prior (a plain crossing means connected in this dataset) points the same way. THE OTHER READING would give 6 nets and a dead branch; rejected.
  S1 (254,315) - non-critical, left at default: a stroke of the '10 Ohm' value label brushing the top of resistor #0's box. Does not change the netlist.

PORTS / CLASSES: no corrections needed. All eight symbols match their drawn class (Resistor x3, Capacitor, Inductor, V-DC, I-DC, GND) and every terminal already sits on a real lead. The unused port candidates flagged by the tracer were each checked in the component montage and are all handwriting brushing a box: (734,422) is the '1' of resistor #1's '10KOhm' label, (743,571)/(743,583) are strokes of the inductor's '5H' label, and (466,566) is the 'Ohm' glyph and its underline from resistor #6's '10KOhm' label. None of them is used by a terminal, which is correct. Two gap bridges exist and neither changes the netlist.

UNRESOLVED: nothing. The drawing is unambiguous once S8 is settled.
